subject: E2E latency triage: hosted vs incumbent — traffic & streaming constraints
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@veridian.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: E2E latency triage: hosted vs incumbent — traffic & streaming constraints

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion on where Veridian's real-world traffic is stressing your current provider. I pulled out the follow-ups and a short ask list so we can scope a focused PoC: 

Recap / goals
- Confirm p95 and p99 E2E targets you care about (app-level, including network, TLS, and client fronting).
- Understand the streaming session behavior (concurrent open streams, per-stream token rate, typical session lengths).
- Get a realistic traffic profile for day-to-day and peak (burst) windows to run our hosted vs incumbent comparison.
- Agree on acceptance criteria for hosted test (latency envelope, error budget, cold-start tolerance).

Concrete asks from Veridian
1) Target SLOs: please confirm numeric targets for p95 and p99 (e.g., p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 450ms).
2) Concurrency: expected steady concurrency and peak concurrency (approx number of concurrent streams and request/sec).
3) Streaming specifics: are you doing streaming on 90% of requests? do you require chunked responses with <50ms chunk spacing?
4) Traffic artifact: a CSV with per-minute qps for a 24-hr window and a representative sample of payload sizes (attach below if possible).

Proposed PoC plan
- Day 0: Redwood runs baseline against your profile (hosted) and we replay against a shadow of your incumbent (you can provide endpoint or we can instrument).
- Day 1–3: sustained ramp and burst tests to capture p95/p99 across real-world tails and cold starts.
- Day 4: run a streaming-focused run for open-stream concurrency and chunk latency.

Attachments: please attach the traffic profile and any existing test harness. I've included a checklist and a suggested payload/load script (attached) we can run if you prefer.

Next steps
- If you can send the CSV and confirm the numeric SLOs by EOD Thursday, we’ll schedule the baseline run for next Monday and share preliminary numbers within 48 hours of the run.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: veridian_traffic_profile.csv (text/csv)]
[Attachment: poc_load_script.sh (text/x-sh)]

From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@veridian.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@veridian.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:13 -0700
Subject: Re: E2E latency triage: hosted vs incumbent — traffic & streaming constraints

Alex — thanks for the concise plan. Quick answers inline: 

Targets
- p95 app-level (end-to-end including TLS): 180ms
- p99 app-level: 520ms

Concurrency
- Steady concurrent open streams: ~180
- Peak concurrent (30 min bursts): ~900
- Avg steady RPS (non-streaming endpoints): 220 rps, bursts up to 1.6k rps

Streaming
- ~70% of product traffic uses streaming. Typical chunk cadence is 30–80ms in production; we need chunk delivery that preserves <=100ms inter-chunk latency for 95% of chunks.

Attachments: sending a sanitized 24-hr per-minute qps file (attached) and a sample payload set. Note that the busiest window is typically 13:00–13:30 PT.

Question for Redwood
1) Can Redwood’s hosted API preserve chunk spacing at scale when we simulate 900 concurrent streams with 70% streaming mix?
2) For the hosted run, will you simulate our TLS termination topology or do you recommend routing through our edge?

We’ll also want an initial compute estimate (vGPU counts) so our infra team can budget.

Sam Ortega
Head of Platform Engineering | Veridian AI
sam.ortega@veridian.ai
[Attachment: veridian_traffic_profile_20270519.csv (text/csv)]

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@veridian.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: E2E latency triage: hosted vs incumbent — traffic & streaming constraints

Appreciate the fast responses and the CSV — that's perfect. Short answers and what we’ll do next: 

1) Chunk spacing at scale
- Yes — our hosted runtime supports sub-100ms chunk emission at scale, but the observed tail depends on prefix distribution and KV cache hit rates. For the PoC we’ll instrument token-level timestamps to verify inter-chunk latency at p95/p99.

2) TLS topology
- Recommendation: terminate TLS at your edge (like you do today) and route to Redwood over mTLS peering for the most representative e2e numbers; we can also run a run where TLS terminates at Redwood to isolate network overhead. Please tell us which you prefer for the first run.

Compute estimate
- Preliminary guidance (very rough): to simulate 900 concurrent streams with 70% streaming mix at your payload sizes, expect ~6–8 A100-eq vGPUs for sustained baseline; bursts will require temporary autoscale capacity (~12 vGPUs) for the 30-min window. We’ll make this concrete after a dry-run.

Runbook and instrumentation
- We’ll run the hosted baseline from our us-west-2 fleet and replay the CSV at your indicated time windows (we can align with your 13:00–13:30 PT peak). We’ll produce a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 token latency, chunk inter-arrival distribution, and error rates.

I’ve uploaded our p95/p99 comparison template and a suggested load script to the shared drive link below. If you prefer, we’ll run both TLS-topology permutations and mark them in the results.

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Veridian/latency-profile
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/8675309/company/Veridian-AI

Thanks — we’ll queue the baseline for Monday pending your TLS preference.

Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 12:18:45 -0700
Subject: Re: E2E latency triage: hosted vs incumbent — traffic & streaming constraints

Looping in a couple operational notes for the PoC: 
- We should capture tracing spans from client edge -> Redwood -> model runtime to attribute network vs infer time.
- Toggle prefix/KV cache on/off during one run to measure delta on tail.
- Add a Canary fallback test: route 10% of traffic to an alternate model variant to validate graceful degradation.

I’ll prep the runbook checklist and sync with infra to reserve the vGPU capacity Alex mentioned.

Ben

From: Elena Park <elena.park@veridian.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@veridian.ai>, Veridian SRE <sre@veridian.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: E2E latency triage: hosted vs incumbent — traffic & streaming constraints

Thanks — two additional asks from compliance and infra: 
1) TLS/Network: if we terminate TLS at your side, can you provide packet-level egress IP ranges and support for strict mTLS? We need those for our firewall rules.
2) Compliance: Veridian requires SOC 2 evidence for any vendor handling production data. We’ve got an NDA to sign; I’ll send the DocuSign link once legal clears.

Also — can you provide a short vGPU sizing note we can attach to the internal budget request? The preliminary numbers Alex gave look reasonable, but we prefer a one-page justification with cost assumptions.

Elena

[Attachment: Veridian_NDA_Docusign_Link (url)]

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@veridian.ai>, Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: E2E latency triage: hosted vs incumbent — traffic & streaming constraints

Great — summary and next steps: 
1) Veridian to confirm TLS topology for first run (terminate at edge + mTLS or terminate at Redwood). Please reply with one-line preference.
2) Veridian to share the final sanitized traffic CSV and confirm the 13:00–13:30 PT window to align our run.
3) Redwood to run two baseline variants if requested (edge-terminated and Redwood-terminated) and provide an artifact with p50/p95/p99 token latency, chunk inter-arrival distribution, error budget consumption, and cold-start incidence.
4) Redwood will upload a one-page vGPU sizing note and the PoC checklist to the shared drive by EOD Friday.

Attachments pushed to shared drive: redwood_p95_p99_matrix.pdf, proof_of_concept_checklist.md

If that looks good, I’ll book the run for Monday 2027-05-24 12:45 PT (to hit your 13:00–13:30 peak) pending your TLS preference.

Thanks all — Alex
